findings.title: O4 RoPE-table build/cache identity across runtimes
findings.plain_language: The op accepted cos/sin tables built anywhere. A table built on the CPU has different last bits than one built on the GPU (about 1 element in 5), which flips ~0.1% of the bf16 outputs. All current callers happen to build on CUDA and all 4 table builders in the repo agree bit-for-bit on CUDA, and the vLLM (CUDA 13.0) and Megatron (CUDA 12.9) envs produce the same table, but nothing enforced it.

evidence_after.cpu_build_error: RuntimeError: contract O4: the RoPE table is built by a fixed fp32 torch-CUDA function; got device cpu. CPU/other-device builds differ in the last bits (~19% of cos/sin elements). Build on the CUDA device that runs the kernel (canonical_rope_table).

findings.fix: rope_table raises RuntimeError on non-CUDA devices; canonical_rope_table(device) (one cached (cos, sin) object per CUDA device, 131072 rows, verify=True checks the pinned sha256); rope_rows(positions) = index_select of it; rope_table_sha256(); trace()['rope_table'] records builder, device_type, formula, sha256.
findings.bits_changed: none (CUDA builds are unchanged; only non-CUDA builds now raise)

findings.title: non-bf16 inputs silently accepted
findings.plain_language: fp32/fp16 q,k ran and returned fp32/fp16 outputs, skipping the contract's single bf16 rounding. Now the strict kernel raises TypeError for anything but bf16.

torch.float32.error: TypeError: the strict qknorm_scaled_rope kernel takes bf16 q/k only (contract O4: bf16 in, one rounding to bf16 at the end); got q torch.float32, k torch.float32. Use qknorm_scaled_rope_fp32/_fp64 for fp32/fp64 references.

torch.float16.error: TypeError: the strict qknorm_scaled_rope kernel takes bf16 q/k only (contract O4: bf16 in, one rounding to bf16 at the end); got q torch.float16, k torch.float16. Use qknorm_scaled_rope_fp32/_fp64 for fp32/fp64 references.

findings.fix: _check_inputs requires q.dtype == k.dtype == bf16 (TypeError); the backward launcher requires bf16 output gradients (TypeError).

findings.title: no TP-parity test for head shards (BLOCK_HQ 16/8/4 vs 32)
findings.plain_language: The coverage gap was real; the kernel itself was already correct. Every TP2/4/8 rank shard (16/8/4 query heads + 1 KV head) gives exactly the bits of the matching slice of the full 32/2-head call, forward and backward, local and global layers: 0 mismatching elements in 84 shard runs (T = 1, 7, 4096). Test added.
findings.fix: test only (TestG2TensorParallelShards); no kernel change needed

findings.title: implicit local/global selection
findings.plain_language: Passing cos=None on a sliding-window layer silently ran the NoPE path (95% of the outputs differ, no error). Callers can now say local=True/False (checked against cos/sin) or use qknorm_scaled_rope_at(q, k, pos, local=|layer_idx=) where the layer kind is mandatory. local=None keeps the old behaviour so existing callers work.

evidence_before.explicit_local_flag: TypeError: qknorm_scaled_rope() got an unexpected keyword argument 'local'

evidence_after.explicit_local_flag: ValueError (fails closed): local=True (sliding-window RoPE layer) needs cos/sin rows; got None

findings.fix: qknorm_scaled_rope(..., local=None|True|False); qknorm_scaled_rope_at(q, k, positions, *, local | layer_idx, check_range=True); layer_is_local(i); trace()['layer_selection'].
findings.residual: local=None (legacy implicit) is still accepted for backward compatibility; the call sites must pass local= (integrator patches) before it can be removed.

findings.title: int32 offset overflow
findings.plain_language: With T >= 524288 tokens (T*32*128 >= 2^31) the element offsets wrapped. Depending on memory layout the old kernel either crashed (illegal memory access) or silently wrote 64 output rows into an unrelated tensor (262,144 elements) and returned garbage rows. Offsets are now int64; no measurable speed change; output bits unchanged for every shape.
